extraction_scope: Worker-6 bounded mechanism adjudication from primary methods/results, Tables 1-3, Figures 3-7, and supplementary Figure S7; phenotype/context claims are not promoted beyond their evidence class.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The p-BthTX-I analogs directly inhibit SARS-CoV-2 PLpro enzymatic activity in vitro, with Table 3 reporting percent inhibition at 10 µM and IC50 values.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: L/D monomer, dimer, and tetramer p-Bth analogs
direct_assay_types: concentration-response curves in Supplementary Figure S7
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports PLpro enzymatic inhibition, not direct proof of antiviral cellular efficacy for every analog in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper tests membrane permeabilization in POPE/POPG and POPC/POPG model vesicles and uses those results as membrane-interaction context for the peptide analogs.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: L/D monomer, dimer, and tetramer p-Bth analogs
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model vesicle leakage is not promoted to a specific intact-cell bacterial molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Circular dichroism experiments evaluate peptide structural behavior in membrane mimetics, LPS, and E. coli total lipid extract, providing biophysical membrane-context evidence.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: L/D monomer, dimer, and tetramer p-Bth analogs
mechanism_claims.limitations: CD shifts are contextual interaction evidence and do not by themselves establish killing mechanism in cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Tables 1 and 2 support the phenotype-level conclusion that dimerization/dendrimerization is important for antibacterial activity of these p-Bth analogs.
mechanism_claims.limitations: MIC/MBC phenotype data support activity and bactericidal/bacteriostatic classification but not a standalone molecular mechanism.
